consumer_seed: The Connected Nations Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
The update reports a snapshot of UK mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
The Spring 2026 publication is an interim update to Connected Nations 2025.
Fixed broadband availability includes fixed-line and fixed-wireless-access networks.
The update also reports take-up of full-fibre services.
Decent broadband is described as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Mobile coverage reporting uses signal-strength predictions supplied by the four mobile network operators.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises in January 2026.
The reported full-fibre residential availability level was 82% of 30.5 million UK homes.
An additional 1.2 million homes gained full-fibre access in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up across residential and commercial premises reached 12.4 million connections.
Full-fibre take-up increased by 1.8 million connections in the six months to January 2026.
The reported take-up equalled 47% of premises with full-fibre access.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89% of UK homes.
The report states that 27.1 million homes had gigabit-capable broadband availability.
The prior July 2025 gigabit-capable level was 87%, or 26.4 million homes.
Individual mobile-network 5G coverage outside premises ranged from 76% to 94%.
Coverage outside premises from all mobile network operators increased from 47% to 64%.
The Map Your Mobile news item was published on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used Map Your Mobile.
Map Your Mobile is described as a free mobile coverage checker.
Users enter a postcode to compare mobile networks in an area.
The checker provides a score showing which company performs best in the postal district.
The service is intended to help compare networks where people live, work or travel.
The checker combines crowdsourced Opensignal information with predictive data from UK mobile networks.
Ofcom says the checker is regularly updated with fresh data.
The checker can indicate whether coverage is likely to work inside a house.
Users can share feedback through the checker.
Map Your Mobile compares 4G and 5G signal.
After postcode entry, the checker provides coverage and performance information.
Coverage results distinguish likely indoor and outdoor availability.
Coverage may be shown as good or variable.
Coverage results are displayed on a map that can be moved and zoomed.
Performance represents the likelihood of streaming video in the local postal district.
Performance dials are displayed separately for each network.
Trees, buildings and wall thickness are identified as factors that can affect coverage.
The Ofcom consumer switch-off guide was published on 6 March 2024.
The guide was last updated on 29 May 2026.
UK 3G mobile networks are now switched off.
UK 2G mobile networks are being switched off gradually over the next few years.
The guide identifies 2G, 4G and 5G as the mobile technologies currently used for UK mobile services.
The 2G switch-off can affect customers using older devices and services.
Customers using 4G or 5G devices are unlikely to be affected, though updates may be needed.
Providers are retiring 2G to make room for 4G and 5G networks.
Mobile network operators have said they will switch off 2G by 2033 at the latest.
2G-only devices will need to be upgraded to at least 4G.
Each mobile network operator sets its own 2G switch-off timetable.
Ofcom advises customers with questions or concerns to contact their mobile provider.
expansion_rule: For each of 37 verified BDUK contracts emit sixteen supplier-aggregate records: supplier contract count, supplier July contracted total, supplier July built total, supplier built ratio, contract share of supplier contracted total, contract share of supplier built total, three within-supplier ranks, three supplier-level ranks, contract July gap, contract share of supplier gap, and built/contracted comparison with supplier medians.
